features.optics-sfp-plus: the two management uplinks are listed only as '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'; the datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types block covers the QSFP-DD field alone, so no module list is published for them and none is inferred
features.optics-sfp28: the datasheet lists the four ports as 1/10/25G SFP28 and its Compatible Transceiver Types block covers only the QSFP-DD field, so no module list is carried for them

gaps.note: UfiSpace has published a hardware installation guide for every other UfiSpace platform modelled in this library and none for the S9620 family. That single absence is behind most of the other entries here: no Component Physical Information table to check the FRU faces against, no front-panel or FRU LED tables, no Port Overview table stating the ID ranges, no space-clearance or grounding section, no rail or pin counts, and no orthographic top, side or bottom elevations. The whole model rests on one datasheet and its two embedded renders.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or any UfiSpace mechanical drawing of this chassis.

gaps.note: the six system lamps sit beside a printed white legend box whose six words are unreadable at every resolution held - 11-px-tall smears at 9.17 px/mm on the only image of them. The names carried on the placements (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID) are the S9321-64E HIG's names for the same six-lamp column on the same vendor's 2RU faceplate, in the order that lamp column runs, and the glyph outlines here are consistent with them. THEY ARE A DIFFERENT PRODUCT'S DOCUMENT, and the reason is filed as sources-disagree rather than needs-photo because the disagreement is between what this device's artwork says (nothing legible) and what a sibling's table says, which is not the same thing as nobody having looked.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel, or the S9620-32E hardware installation guide's front-panel LED table.

gaps.note: not one lamp on this device has a documented meaning. The datasheet tables no LED behaviour at all, and the HIG that would carry the front-panel, PSU FRU and fan FRU LED tables does not exist for this family. So the six system lamps, the 32 per-port lamps, the six SFP-cage lamps and the supply's own lamp all carry positions and no states. Every other UfiSpace device in this library transcribes those tables in full; copying one across from a different SKU would assert this platform's behaviour from another platform's document, and the lamp names above are already one borrowing more than is comfortable.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide, or a NOS LED table.

gaps.note: three unlabelled round openings about 6 mm across - one at (6.89, 48.80) on the front left, two at (430.66, 21.89) and (430.65, 71.54) on the front right - and a 2.0 x 30.9 dark slot at x 431.98-433.94. No legend, no callout, and nothing in the datasheet names them. The S9321-64E carries the identical arrangement and its provenance leaves them unidentified too, so two models have now failed to name the same UfiSpace family feature. They are drawn as dark decor and named here so the marks are recorded unknowns rather than unexplained ink.
gaps.wanted: a hardware installation guide front-panel figure with callouts, or a photograph of the bezel from an angle.

gaps.note: the datasheet orders PSU-322-DEJR-NN (3200W DC, exhaust) beside the AC unit, and both embedded renders show the AC build with C20 inlets. Nothing held shows the DC face. ufispace/psu-322-ac is measured; no psu-322-dc component is built, because every number on it would have been guessed from the AC sibling's outline. The bays accept and default to the AC unit only, and there is no dc configuration - an orderable variant the drawing cannot show is better absent than invented.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the PSU-322-DEJR-NN face.

gaps.note: the datasheet's FAN Types line orders FAN-805616-HCD; ufispace/fan-805616, built for the S9311-64D from that device's HIG, is drawn as FAN-805616-HCE. Both are the exhaust build of the same 805616 family, the face this render shows matches that component's four element offsets to within half a millimetre, and no document held says what the D and E suffixes distinguish. The component is reused rather than duplicated, and the suffix difference is recorded rather than smoothed over.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet or ordering guide covering the 805616 fan family.

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-805616 states no draw; its own contract records the search that established the vendor does not publish one for the 805616 family. This datasheet adds nothing - its only watt figures are the 696 W system typical and the two 3200 W supply nameplates. L29's standing warning is the live record that the chassis module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's rating label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.

gaps.note: the datasheet gives 'Typical power: 696 Watts (no transceiver)' and no maximum. On every other UfiSpace platform here the maximum comes from the HIG's Connecting Power section with its test conditions printed beside it (40 C ambient, optics populated, 100% load); with no HIG there is no such figure and none is derived. Two 3200 W supplies bound what the chassis can draw and say nothing about what it does draw.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-32E hardware installation guide's Connecting Power section.

gaps.note: the left, right and bottom faces are size-only. The isometric shows the left side carrying a rail-kit hole and standoff-pin field, so it is not blank on the hardware, but the only image of it is foreshortened to about 30 degrees with no scale and no HIG sentence to state a count. The right side and the underside appear in no held image. This is what caps the device at capability level 2.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic side elevation, or the rail-installation figure a UfiSpace HIG normally carries.

gaps.note: six stiffening grooves are countable on the isometric render of the cover and their direction is legible; their pitch, length and the cover screw positions are laid out evenly over the stated 580 mm depth and are estimated. The count is the vendor's, the spacing is mine.
gaps.wanted: a top elevation with dimension lines.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices

provenance.attrs: datasheet SPECIFICATIONS, ENVIRONMENTAL, PERFORMANCE, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE and ACCESSORIES blocks, read out of the docling OCR because pdftotext returns nothing from the outlined glyphs. The timing row's own footnotes are carried into the attr rather than dropped: '*NOS integration is necessary to activate the specific feature' and '**Additional license is required' qualify SMPTE ST 2059-2, and the difference between a profile this box supports and one an order has to license is exactly what a compliance-shaped field must not quietly lose.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 580 x 87.7 mm or 17.17' x 22.83' x 3.45", Weight: 19.65kg or 46.42lb (without FRU)'. 436 is the body and not a rack face: on the front render the metal runs x 609-4605 px with two small stubs projecting to 584 and 4622 that are only ~120 px of the 808 px height - rail furniture of the same kind the S9321-64E's provenance describes on that chassis, not ears, and they are not drawn. There is no HIG here to state a rail kit or an ear fold, so the ear-extent sentence that model could write cannot be written for this one; what can be said is that 436 is 46 mm short of a 19-inch rack face and the render shows no flange. Depth 580 is 'without FRU' by the same table's own heading; the fan and PSU handles project beyond it and are carried on the FRU contracts, not in this number.
provenance.extraction: the datasheet's spec text is set as OUTLINED GLYPHS and pdftotext returns nothing from it; the docling conversion recovered it by OCR and doc.md is what the attrs below are transcribed from. The figures likewise: docling's fig-0001/0002 are 660 x 145 and 529 x 130 downsamples, while `pdfimages -png` pulls the ORIGINAL embedded rasters at 5225 x 2934 (front, page 1 object 282) and 6250 x 4419 (rear, page 2 object 85). Every measurement here is off the pdfimages extractions; the docling figures would have given a fifth of the resolution and were not used.
provenance.front-gate1: measured - the embedded front render (5225 x 2934 px) puts the chassis body at x 609-4605, y 1034-1841: 3997 x 808 px for a stated 436 x 87.7 mm. Aspect 4.947 against a true 4.9715, 0.5% out, so it is orthographic and carries geometry at 9.1674 px/mm across and 9.2132 down. It is a RENDER rather than a photograph, which is why it passes a gate photographs almost never do - and also why it can only ever show the build the vendor chose to render.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9620-32E end of life' - no announcement. UfiSpace unveiled the platform at the OCP APAC Summit in August 2025 as the first Broadcom Qumran3D product and lists it as current. none-announced is a checked state, not an absence.
provenance.mgmt-cluster: measured, and named from the datasheet's PHYSICAL list rather than from callouts, because there are no callouts. Left to right along the upper band: a recessed RESET pinhole with a 2.95 mm white ring centred (113.83, 21.60) under a printed RESET; a PORTRAIT USB 3.0 Type-A, shell x 119.23-125.34 y 9.66-22.36 with a blue tongue, under the SS trident (std/usb-a is drawn landscape and is placed rotate: 90, its landed box 120.04-124.54 x 10.01-22.01); a micro-USB console shell x 130.68-137.88 y 20.51-22.57 under IOIOI; an RJ45 console bezel x 142.68-158.17 y 9.01-22.25 under IOIOI; and an RJ45 OOB management bezel x 162.64-178.02 y 9.23-22.15 under an Ethernet icon, with two green lamps inside its own aperture at (164.93, 20.57) and (175.62, 20.57) which are the jack's integrated pair and are not drawn separately. Both RJ45 bezels measure 15.5 x 13.2 and take std/rj45 (16.0 x 14.0) seated on the measured bezel centre - the 20 mm spacing leaves room for the full IEC bezel, so the rj45-ganged part that a tighter block would need is not used here. Both jacks are drawn keyway-DOWN with the contacts at the top, which is the orientation the render shows at 8x and is std/rj45's own default, so neither is rotated.
provenance.port-grid: measured - and THE RULER IS THE PER-PORT LAMPS, not the cage bezels. Each port carries a blue label patch on its left with the port numeral and one green lamp; the 16 lamps of the lower row fit x = 23.381 + 25.3087 j with individual steps of 25.28-25.33, and the upper row's 16 fit the same line. The drawn cage bezels give a first-to-last span of 26.50 to 405.24+17.56 which agrees with the lamp grid end to end, but their individual left edges scatter by up to a millimetre because the render antialiases a 0.4 mm white outline, so the cage x here are COMPUTED from the lamp grid and are not read off the bezels. std/qsfp-dd's registry 19.0 x 10.0 opening is seated centred on each drawn bezel centre (34.30 + 25.3087 j); the drawn bezel measures 17.35 wide, which is the visible outline inside the MSA opening rather than a different number for it.
provenance.port-leds: measured - one green lamp per port on its blue patch, 32 of them, at x = 23.38 + 25.3087 j with y centres 52.17 (upper row) and 66.15 (lower). Each is about 1.2 mm across in the render; drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, the nearest library part, and a compromise recorded here rather than hidden). One further lamp sits centred above each of the six SFP cages at y centre 10.31, on the cage pitch. NOTHING STATES WHAT ANY OF THESE 38 LAMPS SHOW - see gaps; they carry positions and no states.
provenance.port-numbering: measured off the render at 4x zoom - the blue patches print 0 and 1 in the first column, 2 and 3 in the second, with the even numeral always in the upper row. So column j carries ports 2j (top) and 2j+1 (bottom), 0-31. The four SFP28 cages are numbered 32, 33, 34, 35 on their own yellow legend strip, continuing the QSFP-DD range; the two SFP+ management cages left of them are numbered 0 and 1 in a separate namespace under a bracket carrying an Ethernet icon, which is what makes them management rather than the 32-35 traffic ports. THERE IS NO PORT OVERVIEW TABLE TO CHECK THIS AGAINST - a UfiSpace HIG normally states the ID ranges in words, and here the artwork is the only statement of them.
provenance.port-rows: measured - two rows, 16 columns. The cage bezels' own white top and bottom lines sit at y 46.67/55.79 (upper row) and 62.08/71.42 (lower), a row pitch of 15.41, and the blue label patches give 46.35 and 61.65, a pitch of 15.30. The apertures are placed at 46.40 and 61.81. THE ROWS ARE NOT MIRRORED AND THE LABEL PATCHES ARE: within the upper patch the numeral is above the lamp and within the lower one it is below, so the two lamps of a column sit 13.98 apart rather than the 15.41 of the rows - that difference is the mirror, measured, not assumed. The cage art itself is symmetric top to bottom (cross-correlating the upper cage against the flipped lower one scores 0.952 against 0.972 the same way up), so no port carries rotate: 180, unlike the belly-to-belly bands of the S9321-64E where the seam is visible.
provenance.power: datasheet - 'Typical power: 696 Watts (no transceiver)', and the scope is the vendor's own parenthesis. THERE IS NO MAXIMUM. Every other UfiSpace platform in this library gets its maximum from the HIG's Connecting Power section with the test conditions printed beside it; this device has no HIG, so power-max-w is simply absent and power-envelope is 'bare' because 'no transceiver' is what the vendor said the 696 W covers. The feed figures 'AC input: 200 to 240V, 16A' and 'DC input: -48 to -60V, 80A' are the INPUT to provision per supply and are recorded as input, not as draw - the C100G lesson. Nothing here adds the two PSU nameplates or the fan modules to 696 and calls the result anything.
provenance.rear-fans: measured, and the pitch is corroborated four ways rather than eyeballed. Four repeated features - the red release tab, the red airflow badge, the green status lamp and the red tube handle - give first-to-last steps of 84.02, 83.97, 83.91 and 83.97, so the fan pitch is 84.0. The module face's own top and bottom seams read y 3.30 and 83.92, a height of 80.62. THAT IS ufispace/fan-805616 AND THE MATCH IS WHAT IDENTIFIES IT: laying that component's own element offsets (badge 7.8/4.1, lamp 12.3/18.4, handle 27.0/21.6, tab 0.8/30.2 - measured by another agent off the S9311-64D HIG, not by me) over this render puts the face origin at (3.05, 3.70) with a spread of 0.5 mm across four independent features, and its stated 83.7 x 80.0 face then fits the measured 84.0 pitch and 80.6 height. The datasheet orders FAN-805616-HCD where that component is drawn as FAN-805616-HCE; both are the exhaust build of the same 805616 family and no document held here distinguishes them - see gaps.
provenance.rear-gate1: measured - the embedded rear render (6250 x 4419 px) puts the body at x 1709-4467, y 2071-2628: 2759 x 558 px for 436 x 87.7 mm. Aspect 4.944 against a true 4.9715, 0.55% out, so 6.328 px/mm across and 6.363 down. Four fan modules and two stacked PSUs.
provenance.rear-legends: measured - the chassis strip right of the PSUs carries a yellow warning label (x 419.09-434.10, y 5.66-47.31, reading REMOVE LABEL FOR SYSTEM GROUNDING set vertically), an earth symbol below it at about (423.0, 48.6), then PSU0 at y 60.82-64.43 and PSU1 at y 67.74-71.04, then FAN at y 77.32-80.62 with 0|1|2|3 beneath. PSU0 and PSU1 are printed one above the other in that strip rather than beside their bays, which reads oddly and is what the render shows at 8x. The airflow badge, the status lamp legend and the model plate on each FRU belong to that FRU's own skin and are not repeated here.
provenance.rear-psus: measured - two supplies stacked, faces x 343.55-416.75 and y 3.77-43.57 / 45.89- 85.49, so 73.2 x 39.8 on a 42.12 pitch. That is the CRPS envelope and it is a DIFFERENT FACE from the library's other UfiSpace CRPS supply: psu-242-ac puts its status lamp below the latch and crosses its fan frame with a pull bar, and this one puts the lamp ABOVE the latch at y 7.1-9.6 and carries two captive Phillips screws instead. So ufispace/psu-322-ac was built for this device from this device's own render rather than skinned off that one. The matched-scale comparison also showed the vendor drawing the C20's three blade slots as vertical bars on a body that is turned on its side, which no rotated connector does; the arrangement agrees exactly and the slot aspect is left to the standard part, recorded on that contract. The AC build is the only build rendered; the datasheet also orders PSU-322-DEJR-NN and that face is not modelled - see gaps.
provenance.sfp-block: measured - six cages in one silver ganged shell, x 182.17-268.02, y 12.59-22.58. Six lamps above them at x centres 189.51, 203.69, 217.87, 232.18, 246.36, 260.65 give a pitch of 14.23, and the shell's own span divided by six gives 14.31; the cages are laid out on std/sfp-ganged's own 14.25 width, centred on the shell, which puts cage 0's centre at 189.47 against the lamp's 189.51. The shell is DRAWN 0.5 mm taller than measured (12.35 for 10.5) so the registry's 10.4 mm apertures sit inside their own bright shell instead of 0.2 mm proud of it - said here because the 9.99 is the measurement and the 10.5 is not.
provenance.sides-and-bottom: deliberately size-only, and each for its own reason. The isometric shows the LEFT side carrying a scattered field of holes and standoff pins for a rail kit, so that face is not blank on the hardware - but it is foreshortened to about 30 degrees in the only image that shows it, no count survives the perspective, and there is no HIG text to state one (the S9321-64E could write 'the chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side' because its guide says so; nothing here does). Drawing an estimated pin row would be inventing a mounting pattern. The RIGHT side appears in no image at all. The BOTTOM appears in no image at all. AXIS CONVENTION, recorded because these faces carry nothing that could expose it: on a RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT and on a LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, and a bottom view mirrors left and right. Three size-only faces is what L45 will report and it is the honest state.
provenance.sources: THIS DEVICE HAS NO HARDWARE INSTALLATION GUIDE. UfiSpace has published one for every other UfiSpace platform in this library and none for the S9620 family, so everything a HIG normally supplies is missing here: the Component Physical Information table, the front-panel and FRU LED tables, the Port Overview table, the space-clearance and grounding sections, the rail and pin counts, and every orthographic elevation. What is held is ONE document - the S9620-32E datasheet (2025-06-30, sha256 5ae2cb2a...) - plus three vendor product photographs. The photographs are the SAME RENDERS the datasheet embeds, at 520 x 150 instead of 5225 x 2934, so they are one source wearing two hats and are NOT a second reading; only the isometric s9620-32e-1-view.png shows anything the datasheet does not, namely the top cover and one foreshortened side. Where a number below says 'measured', it was measured on the datasheet's own embedded render, and there is nothing else in the intake to check it against.
provenance.system-leds: measured - six lamps in a vertical column at x 12.33-15.38, five green and the sixth blue, beside a white legend box at x 15.82-19.97 y 39.83-55.35 carrying six dark legends. Lamp centres 41.46, 43.85, 46.35, 48.79, 51.34 and 53.78: measured gaps 2.39/2.50/2.44/2.55/2.44, drawn on those measured centres because the scatter is under a tenth of the pitch. Each lamp is a 3.05 x 1.95 rectangle on the hardware; common/led-rect is 4.6 x 2.6 and cannot sit on a 2.46 pitch without overlapping its neighbour, so common/led-dot (2.0) is used - the right pitch in the wrong shape, recorded rather than nudged. THE LEGEND STRINGS ARE UNREADABLE: at 9.17 px/mm the six words are 11-px-tall smears. The S9321-64E's HIG prints SYNC/SYS/FAN/PS0/PS1/ID for the same six-lamp column beside the same kind of box on the same vendor's 2RU faceplate, and the glyph outlines here are consistent with that reading, but this device has no such table and the names carried here are therefore BORROWED FROM A SIBLING'S DOCUMENT and are filed as a gap. The lamps' state vocabulary is not borrowed - the placements carry no states at all.
provenance.timing-cluster: measured - two yellow SMB bulkheads at the far left, bezel washers 7.9 mm across centred (9.22, 21.70) and (9.28, 35.60), each under its printed legend (1PPS above the upper, 10MHZ above the lower). Drawn with std/smb (4.83 mm, registry) on the measured centres with the yellow washer as decor behind, because the registry sizes the connector and the 7.9 mm yellow is the ring around it - the same construction the S9321-64E uses, and said so here because the sentence is that model's.
provenance.top: photo-derived COUNT, estimated SPACING - and this is the clearest single cost of having no HIG. The only view of the cover is the isometric s9620-32e-1-view.png at 650 x 278, a three-quarter render with no dimension lines and no orthographic equivalent anywhere in the intake. Six long recessed stiffening grooves are countable in it and they run across the width, spaced along the depth, which is the same arrangement the S9321-64E's HIG dimensions on the same vendor's 2RU cover - that sibling is where the READING of the direction was checked, and it is not where the six came from. The pitch, the groove length and the screw positions are ESTIMATED, laid out evenly over the 580 mm depth. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, the convention the other UfiSpace top faces in this library use.
provenance.unidentified-openings: UNIDENTIFIED, recorded not resolved. Three round openings about 6 mm across, drawn black and carrying no legend, sit at (6.89, 48.80) on the left and (430.66, 21.89) and (430.65, 71.54) on the right, plus a 2.0 x 30.9 dark slot at x 431.98-433.94. The S9321-64E carries the same arrangement - one unlabelled 6.8 mm circle at the left, two at the right and a narrow right-hand slot - and its provenance also leaves them unidentified, so this is a UfiSpace family feature that two models have now failed to name rather than a reading peculiar to this one. Drawn as dark decor so the panel is not silently missing them, and named in gaps.
provenance.vents: measured - a honeycomb field across the upper left (x 5.02-87.16, full height y 6.19-13.69 and narrowing to x 14.40 for y 13.69-21.39, with a single hex column continuing down x 14.40-17.56 to y 38.75), a second honeycomb block at the lower left (x 6.22-18.87, y 62.30-83.25), and slot-vent columns on the port pitch above the upper row (y 30.50-45.70) and below the lower row (y 72.61-80.10), each 20.29 wide starting at x 25.20 + 25.3087 j, plus a hex band across the top of the SFP shell at x 181.70-268.70 y 6.20-12.35. Drawn as vent decor; the hex and slot cell geometry is the renderer's, not the vendor's. The face itself samples #252525 on the render and that is what chassis.color carries - the first pass left it to the renderer's default and the matched-scale comparison showed a panel several shades too light, which is exactly the kind of thing only looking finds.
